summary: Twin jungle falls deep in Purna sanctuary. Raja and Rani drop within sight of each other, earned by a proper monsoon forest trek.
description:
Raja Rani is Purna sanctuary's secret pair: two waterfalls (Raja and Rani, locally Pandar Dhodh) that stand apart in the forest yet within view of each other, so that from the rock apron of one you watch the other threading down its own face. Few of Dang's falls offer that composition, and fewer still take this much forest to reach.

The reach is the filter. Approaches run from Savarkhadi on the Ahwa side or Dhongi Amba on the Vyara side toward Daradi village, and the final stretch is a genuine jungle trek inside sanctuary forest, braiding paths, stream beds, leech country in the rains. A local from the approach villages is not a luxury here; the falls are not signed and the sanctuary prefers walkers accounted for.

July to September is the window that justifies the effort, when both falls run full and the forest is loud with water. Treat it as a trekking day, not a picnic stop, and leave the pools alone in spate.
highlights: Twin falls, each visible from the other's viewing rocks
Among the least-visited of Dang's named waterfalls
history_legend: The paired falls carry a king-and-queen naming, Raja and Rani, common to twin natural features across India; locally the site is equally known as Pandar Dhodh.

modes.road: Via Savarkhadi from the Ahwa side, or Dhongi Amba from the Vyara side, toward Daradi village; the last leg is on foot
modes.rail: Waghai (heritage narrow gauge); Bilimora Jn for broad gauge

access.last_mile: Jungle trek from the road end through sanctuary forest. Paths braid; take a local
access.road_condition: Village tar then forest track; monsoon slows everything

booking.notes: Inside Purna sanctuary, check position with the forest office at Mahal or Ahwa before a monsoon trek

visit.notes: A trekking outing, not a drive-up stop; start early and be out of the forest well before dark.

seasonality.notes: Both falls need the rains; by late autumn the pair thins to streaks.

experience.photography_notes: The one-fall-from-the-other frame is the shot; a mid-zoom carries it better than wide glass in the forest gloom.

amenities.food: None anywhere near. Carry the day's food and water
amenities.guides: Effectively required, arrange in the approach villages (Savarkhadi/Daradi side)

warnings: Sanctuary interior with no network, never trek alone or unannounced
Leeches and slick rock throughout the monsoon window
Stay out of the plunge pools in spate: there is no rescue here

emergency.notes: Inform the forest chowki of your route

tips: Hire a local at the trailhead village: the paths braid and the falls are unsigned
Pair the trek with a Mahal campsite night rather than attempting a same-day return to Saputara
Go mid-week; even small groups change the feel of a place this quiet

faqs.q: Why is it called Raja Rani?
faqs.a: The twin falls are named as a royal pair, Raja and Rani, because they drop within sight of each other across the forest. Locally the site is also called Pandar Dhodh.
